title: Shifting support for non-Congress governments
body: After the 1989 elections no party had a majority. The National Front, an alliance of the Janata Dal and some regional parties, formed the government with outside support from the BJP and the Left Front, which wanted to keep the Congress out of power. In 1996 the United Front, again made up of the Janata Dal and several regional parties, formed the government; this time the Congress and the Left supported it to keep the BJP out of power. Many of the regional parties in these fronts represented the Dalit and backward castes and powerful regional assertion. Political scientists note that the Congress itself had long been a coalition of different interests and social groups, and that since the late 1960s various sections had been leaving it to form their own parties.
